newsitem.title: USA: Italy's Dini plays down hard left's welfare threat.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini plays down hard left's welfare threat.

text.p: Italy's foreign minister Lamberto Dini on Sunday played down threats by the hard left Communist Refoundation party to withdraw support for the government if it does not drop a social welfare reform plan.

"It isn't the first time that Communist Refoundation uses tones that are ... a bit aggressive. The important thing is that unions and industry representatives sit at a table and look for corrective measures to our social welfare system," Dini told reporters while attending a summit of the Group of Seven major industrial nations.
Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti issued the threat in an interview with Turin Daily La Stampa, published on Sunday.

"Communist Refoundation accepted the guidelines of the three-year economic and financial plan (to the year 2000) which indicates precisely that the government's target ... is to limit growth in social spending to GDP growth, so that social spending does not rise more than the nation's wealth," Dini said. Last week the centre-left coalition government headed by

Prime Minister Romano Prodi submitted a document on social welfare reform to the unions, stating that social spending must remain within GDP growth limits. That would entail around 15 trillion lire's worth of spending cuts in 1998.
Prodi's government relies on support in the lower house of parliament from Communist Refoundation.
Prodi said last week that the welfare reform plan was only a discussion paper and that no reform will be carried out without the consensus of the unions.
